components.text: Does it fit your week
Your week with an electric car
What counts is not the brochure figure but the range on a cold January morning.
Your 55 km a day are a non-issue even in winter. You would charge about every 4 days.
In the cold consumption rises to 20.6 kWh/100 km. In summer it is 323 km.
The honest figure: cold, at motorway cruising speed. Plan long trips against this one and they hold up.

Charging
Where you charge decides what it costs
At your mileage, the gap between the cheapest and the dearest way to charge is a multiple of any difference between cars.
Moving from “Public charging only” to “Charging at work” saves you about €1,787 a year – more than most choices of car are worth.

What it costs
Over 4 years
Every item on its own – depreciation, energy, servicing, insurance, tax and the German GHG credit.
With how you charge today the electric car is more expensive overall – about €40 a month. With charging of your own that reverses.
Electricity €11.37 against fuel €11.39.
Calculated on the German grid mix. With your own solar or a green tariff it comes out better.

components.text: Your question
Is an electric car practical without a wallbox?
The honest answer: practical yes, economic not at the moment. Your distances are not the problem — the price of charging is.
Your next step
Your route to driving electric
Everything we discussed, on one page.
What I recommend for you
Settle the charging question first, not the car question. With somewhere to charge at home or at work, switching becomes clearly cheaper for you than the car you drive today.
In favour

- Your distances are entirely unremarkable for an electric car
- Where you charge is worth around €1,800 a year
- A compact car covers your profile completely
Still to clarify

- Is a wallbox technically possible at your parking space?
- Does your employer offer charging?
